previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and recurrent febrile episodes was admitted for evaluation of fever, chills, and myalgias recurring every six weeks. He also reported new-onset dysuria and urinary urgency. Initial workup showed mild leukocytosis, normal renal and liver function, and negative urine and blood cultures. Imaging revealed mild intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation raising a radiographic concern for cholangitis, but clinically this was deemed unlikely due to absence of fever, normal labs, and negative cultures. CT chest showed nonspecific ground-glass opacities, likely chronic, with no respiratory symptoms. CMV viral load was negative. The patient remained afebrile throughout admission and improved symptomatically. He was discharged home on his baseline immunosuppressive and prophylactic medications with plans for close follow-up in the liver clinic and outpatient echocardiography to evaluate a new holosystolic murmur.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ man who is currently ___ years status post liver 
transplant for cryptogenic cirrhosis with recent 
hospitalizations for fever of unclear source now admitted for 
recurrent fever, presumed biliary source.  

ACUTE ISSUES:
=============
# Fever, Presumed Recurrent Cholangitis: Pt has a history of 
recurrent fevers with negative workups, and presented after 
multiple fevers at home to >101.  Notably, pt was afebrile and 
without a leukocytosis on presentation.  CXR did not demonstrate 
pneumonia, and blood and urine cultures were negative.  There 
was primarily concern for cholangitis given pt's history of 
biliary anastamotic stricture with stenting.  Pt was initially 
treated with meropenem and vancomycin.  ERCP was performed which 
demonstrated improvement in the previously noted anastamotic 
stricture with good biliary flow.  Pt's previous stents were 
removed without replacement.  Finally, two stones and a small 
amount of sludge were removed. Pt's antibiotics were changed to 
ciprofloxacin with plans for a total 10 day course of 
antibiotics.
